subject: Re: VPC endpoints / IP allowlist / egress & mTLS — next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@finpay.com>
Cc: Sanaa Rahman <sana.rahman@finpay.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: VPC endpoints / IP allowlist / egress & mTLS — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex / Sanaa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to hear more about FinPay's roadmap for embedding LLM features into your payments console. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up an architecture workshop with your infra team: 

What we heard:
- You need private connectivity from your VPCs to Redwood to meet compliance: VPC endpoints or customer-managed NAT egress with IP allowlist.
- mTLS between your egress proxy and our VPC endpoint is preferred for mutual auth.
- DNS resolution and egress to external model artifacts (occasionally) must be controlled — you'd prefer explicit allowlist rules and private DNS where possible.
- Primary workload: chat + structured tool-calling and embeddings-based reranking for transaction enrichment. Low latency is critical for in-product flows.

Immediate next steps I suggest:
1) Share the attached network diagram + IP allowlist template (attached) with your infra/security lead.
2) Please confirm if you require: (a) AWS VPC Endpoint (interface) to Redwood private service in your region, or (b) Egress via your managed NAT with static IPs.
3) Confirm mTLS preference: client cert auth to Redwood endpoint vs. using customer-managed proxy + API key inside private network.
4) Schedule a technical architecture call — proposed times: Tue 5/18 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 5/19 13:00-14:00 PT.

From a Redwood side, I'll bring our Solutions Engineer (Marissa) and our network architect (Jonas) to walk through SDK integration, auth patterns, routing fallbacks, and embeddings serving + reranker topology.

Notes on integration concerns to prepare for the call:
- SDK setup: Our SDK supports init-with-api-key or init-with-mTLS (client cert). We can push a lightweight sidecar (no root perms) if you want to avoid changing app-level credentials.
- Auth & routing: We recommend routing internal traffic to a regional endpoint pinned to a model variant. For failover we'll propose a cost-tiered routing policy (same API surface, different model).
- Embeddings/reranker: For reranking we recommend a small in-VPC cache + prefix KV caching on our side to keep latency sub-100ms for 128-token queries.
- Structured output / tool calling: We’ll demo how function/tool calling is surfaced in the SDK and how webhooks can be routed to your internal endpoints via a private NAT.

Attachments: redwood-network-diagram-v1.pdf, ip_allowlist-template.csv

If that all sounds right, I'll lock in Tue 5/18 10:00 PT.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@finpay.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanaa Rahman <sana.rahman@finpay.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints / IP allowlist / egress & mTLS — follow-up and next steps

Lauren — thanks for the summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) We prefer option (b) — egress via our managed NAT with static elastic IPs — because our security stack sits on the egress proxy and we need to enforce outgoing DPI. We can provide 3 static IPs.
2) mTLS: our compliance team prefers mTLS for the control plane between egress proxy and provider. We'll likely want mutual client certs, rotated by our PKI.
3) DNS: we use a private hosted zone with conditional forwards. Ideally Redwood can accept requests over the NAT IPs and we can avoid exposing any public endpoints.

A couple of asks before the architecture call: 
- Can you confirm whether Redwood supports accepting traffic from a fixed set of external IPs (your side) AND whether you can present a service cert for the endpoint (we will present a client cert)?
- Any guidance on port/IP ranges for the VPC endpoint or just standard HTTPS 443?

We'll take Tue 5/18 10:00 PT if that works for your team. I’ll invite our infra lead.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPay
alex.martinez@finpay.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sanaa Rahman <sana.rahman@finpay.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints / IP allowlist / egress & mTLS — follow-up and next steps

Alex — perfect, thanks for the clarity. Short answers and what we'll bring to the call: 

- Static IPs: Yes — Redwood supports allowinglist by source IP for customer NAT egress. We will need the 3 elastic IPs you provide; we’ll whitelist them on our firewall.
- Service cert: Redwood can present a provider TLS certificate for the endpoint. For mutual TLS, we support client cert validation against your CA. We’ll exchange CSR/CA details in the secure channel (we can use your S3 share or a signed zip via our secure upload).
- Ports: Standard HTTPS 443 only. No extra ports required.

Integration notes we’ll cover on the call (so your infra folks can prep):
1) SDK/auth patterns:
   - Option A (mTLS): SDK connects to https://private.redwood.rw (or region-specific host). SDK configured with client cert + key (stored in your egress proxy). No API key needed at runtime; calls authenticated by mTLS.
   - Option B (API key inside private network): SDK uses API key (rotated) and calls over the NAT IP. We recommend short-lived keys and a small sidecar to perform key rotation.
2) Routing/fallbacks:
   - We'll show our routing policy UI: primary to low-latency regional model, fallback to a compatible quantized variant in another region if health check fails.
3) Embeddings & rerankers:
   - For high-QPS reranking, run embeddings requests via our private endpoint and use our batch endpoints. We recommend enabling prefix caching for your most common queries. We'll propose a cache hit % and expected token cost.
4) Structured outputs / tool-calling:
   - Tool-calls can be returned as structured JSON; we’ll show how to deliver those to an internal webhook behind your egress proxy. We also support signed webhook payloads for integrity.

Attachments: I’ve reattached the network diagram and an IP allowlist CSV with our suggested ranges for egress to Redwood-managed S3/model artifact hosts (only needed if you allow direct model fetches).

We’ll plan to demo the mTLS SDK init and the reranker topology in the architecture call. Marissa and Jonas will handle the deep tech details.

See you Tue 5/18 10:00 PT — I have the invite pending and will send once Alex confirms attendees.

Best,
Lauren

Attachments: redwood-network-diagram-v1.pdf, ip_allowlist-template.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@finpay.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Sanaa Rahman <sana.rahman@finpay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints / IP allowlist / egress & mTLS — next steps + architecture call prep

Hi Alex / team — looping in Jonas (network architect) and myself as the SE for the call. A few practical items to accelerate the workshop: 

Pre-call checklist for FinPay infra (if you can have these ready it will speed the workshop):
- List of the 3 NAT static IPs (so we can pre-configure firewall allowlist on our side).
- TLS client cert chain or CA info (if you want mTLS) and cert rotation cadence requirements.
- Sample private DNS entries you use for conditional forwarding (so we can validate DNS resolution behavior in our staging VPC).
- Expected QPS for chat and reranking (p95 latency SLO target). Numbers like 50 QPS chat, 30 QPS embeddings are helpful.

What we’ll demo on the call:
- mTLS SDK init (two variants: client-side cert in egress proxy, or sidecar with rotated key).
- Routing policy UI + canary failover example (how to pin a customer to a model variant and fallback rules).
- Embeddings batching + reranker architecture (how we keep latency low and cost predictable).
- Webhook delivery through private NAT and payload signature verification.

Action: Alex — if you confirm Tue 5/18 10:00 PT, I’ll send a calendar invite with the proposed agenda and a short pre-meeting form for the infra details above.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
